title: Complaint of TE Eliot Lee vs. Korean Eastern Presbytery
disposition_detail: The complaint was sustained and KEP’s decision annulled in whole. All actions and decisions by the Pulpit Commission acting for HKPC’s Session or church were annulled; KEP must return expended HKPC funds if the congregation requests.
first_summary: Lee challenged Presbytery’s authorization of its Pulpit Commission to act for HKPC’s Session. The SJC sustained the complaint, annulled Presbytery’s decision and the Commission’s resulting actions, and directed return of expended church funds if the congregation requested. Presbytery had acted without the Session’s request or the congregation’s consent, contrary to the constitutional right of a congregation to elect or consent to those governing it.
summary: Lee challenged Presbytery’s authorization of its Pulpit Commission to act for HKPC’s Session. The SJC sustained the complaint, annulled Presbytery’s decision and the Commission’s resulting actions, and directed return of expended church funds if the congregation requested. Neither the Session nor congregation had requested or consented to that authority. The ruling distinguished the Commission’s valid appointment to receive stated-supply requests from its impermissible empowerment to function as the Session or pulpit committee.

sources.supports: Issue, judgment, adopted reasoning, annulment, conditional reimbursement, and distinction between appointing and empowering the Commission.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: The combined heading identifies SJC 2007-09 and 2007-10 (printed p. 132, lines 13–14); section IV.A identifies 2007-09 and states its disposition (printed p. 137, lines 158–168).
evidence_notes.dispute: The issue was KEP’s authorization of the Pulpit Commission to act for HKPC’s Session (printed p. 136, lines 144–148).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: The SJC annulled the Commission’s actions and conditionally ordered return of HKPC funds; KEP lacked Session and congregational consent and could not act for or enlarge the Session or serve unilaterally as pulpit committee (printed p. 136–137, lines 150–166).
evidence_notes.qualifications: The SJC had upheld the Commission’s appointment but expressly had not approved its later actions; its proper original role was receiving Session requests concerning stated supply (printed pp. 136, 138, lines 138–142, 179–187).
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: The supplied history gives the prior adopted SJC judgment upholding appointment of the Commission while reserving later actions (printed p. 136, lines 120–142); no material incorporated result is missing.

source_limits: The source combines cases 2007-09 and 2007-10 and includes a separate concurrence. This synopsis isolates the majority disposition and reasoning for 2007-09.
